text: The court reviewed whether charitable contribution deductions over $250 were allowable under section 170. For each contribution of $250 or more, the taxpayer must obtain a contemporaneous written acknowledgment from the donee that meets the requirements of section 170(f)(8), including a statement whether the donee provided any goods or services in consideration for the contribution. An acknowledgment that omits the required statement does not satisfy the statute.

A later substitute letter from the church, obtained after the taxpayer filed the return, was not treated as contemporaneous for purposes of section 170(f)(8). The court emphasized strict compliance with the substantiation rules for cash contributions when the amount of any single contribution is $250 or more.

The opinion addresses noncash charitable contribution deductions for multiple years and whether the taxpayer met substantiation requirements under section 170, including written acknowledgments and appraisal rules where applicable. The court also considered accuracy-related penalties under section 6662.

Petitioner sought an award of reasonable litigation or administrative costs under section 7430 and Tax Court Rule 231. The underlying deficiency proceeding had involved whether losses from a thoroughbred activity were limited as passive activity losses under section 469.
